title: Titus Andronicus starring Patrick Page #titusandronicus #patrickpage ...
transcript: In the bloodiest of Shakespearean bloodbaths, Titus Andronicus is a revenge tragedy where violence is cyclical and cruelty is the point. This version stars Patrick Page in the titular role, but he's not the only one giving a notable performance. I felt like everyone in this production did a great job balancing the visceral and tragic elements of the story with the humor and even ridiculousness that's embedded in the play. Combined with a modern and cold aesthetic, this gave it a lot of urgency and I found connections to much of today's discourse on masculinity and patriarchy. Aside from the obvious themes of revenge, betrayal, and grief, which are found in pretty much all of Shakespeare's tragedies, paternity is also surfaced a lot in this one. With the backdrop of men continually throughout history starting wars and treating others like property, this play confronts, as if posing, “how can you be so protective of your own kin, yet so willing to commit or cosign the destruction of someone else's?” Having not been previously familiar with this play, I was able to follow it easily enough and it moved pretty well. I knew from the key art that it would be a violent tragedy, but I totally underestimated just how violent it would be. If gore on stage is something you struggle with, you should probably sit this one out. Otherwise, strap in for the ride. With that, another program for my collection.
reasoning: Strong endorsement of performances, direction, and thematic resonance with only a content warning about gore as a caveat. The 'strap in for the ride' framing and praise for the entire cast signals clear recommendation.
